Most Mauritian businesses close their sales on WhatsApp. Very few measure them.

In my last article I called our online market a digitalised bazaar: sellers take buyers from a TikTok live straight into WhatsApp and close the deal by hand. It works, but it is chaos. Missed messages, forgotten follow ups and no idea which ad brought in the sale.

So I wrote the follow up: how to run WhatsApp Business properly.

I cover when the free app is enough and when you need the WhatsApp Business Platform, how to turn labels into a simple sales pipeline, why ads that click to WhatsApp only work if someone answers fast, and what Meta's rules say about opt in before you send a single promotion.

The part most people skip is measurement. If you cannot connect a chat to a sale, you cannot tell which marketing pays. Even a simple log beats guessing.

Your customers already want to buy on WhatsApp. The question is whether you run it like a stall or like a business.
